rv.q: There, the true genius of Baldwin and Buckley at Cambridge is revealed.
Elevator Repair Service may be conducting an experiment pitting style against substance, in which case the former distressingly wins.
Better to recall that the memorable Cambridge debate also happened and is importantly remembered here in only slightly compromised form.

Alas, after Stevenson stops speaking, Sargeant and Williams walk on stage to begin the real debate — very traditional casting here — and the “Baldwin & Buckley at Cambridge” falls back to earth with a thud.
If your goal is to savor Baldwin’s response, mull it over, plumb its depths, you may need to resort to the historical record or better yet YouTube, where the exchange is preserved for posterity.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this verbatim recreation of the historic 1965 debate, with some finding it mesmerizing while others question why not just watch the YouTube video, citing flattened affect that diminishes the orators' power.
